key_insight: Agent success on a task does not guarantee we can identify which product decision the user would prefer, so the paper audits decision uncertainty separately from execution accuracy.
engineering_relevance: For AI product and agent systems, the work suggests preserving decision-relevant structured inputs and explaining why a decision is unresolved before collecting more telemetry.
method: Defines a decision-specific audit from a declared observation channel and product-value contrast.
Computes compatible intervals and witness populations using identification and decision theory.
Adds an executable measurement workflow plus an offline viewer and source-labeled decision receipt.
evidence_signal: In a frozen experiment with 4,800 requests to two pinned model snapshots, all 36 conservative primary intervals remained unresolved; a follow-up with 2,400 calls and supplied preferences resolved 3 of 9 comparisons per model, while a deterministic extractor resolved 7 of 9 without model calls.
watch_item: Unresolved intervals may reflect structural ambiguity, weak identification, or calibration limits, so implementation must avoid treating model-generated reports as ground truth.
paper_title: The Delegation Blind Spot: Auditing Product Decisions from Agent Choices
